description:
Extract data points from plot images in the literature archive. Requested by the maintainer 2026-08-11.

WHY THIS IS NEEDED AND NOT A TOY: several validation targets this project depends on exist ONLY as figures. docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md records that the HTR-10 safety demonstration tests (loss of forced cooling without scram, rod withdrawal without scram) should be expected as digitised plots rather than tabulated data, and the same is true of the MSRE reactivity-insertion figures noted in vtb-findings.md. Without a digitiser those benchmarks cannot be used at all.

THREE INTERFACES, one engine:
- CLI - FULLY AUTOMATIC, no human in the loop. Detects axes, calibrates, traces curves, emits points. This is the agent-facing path and must be scriptable and deterministic.
- TUI (ratatui) - HYBRID: automatic pass first, then human verification and correction.
- egui - HYBRID: automatic pass first, then human verification and correction, with a graphical interface modelled on https://www.graphreader.com/ - load image, set two reference points per axis, choose linear or log per axis, auto-trace the curve, then drag/add/delete individual points, and export.

The automatic-first-then-verify shape is the point: the machine does the tedious part, the human confirms it, and the confirmation is recorded rather than assumed.

MANDATORY OUTPUT REQUIREMENT: every digitisation records its own provenance - source document and figure number, axis calibration reference points, linear/log per axis, reading uncertainty, whether the points were auto-traced or hand-placed or corrected, and by whom and when. Under DATA_POLICY.md digitisation is a processing step and must be documented as one. An exported dataset with no calibration record is not usable as validation evidence.

GOLDEN ORACLE: the sibling bead covers the maintainer supplying hand-digitised points from the Tobias decay-heat figures. Those are the acceptance test - the digitiser output must be compared against them with a stated tolerance, and log axes must be checked specifically because that is where naive pixel interpolation goes wrong.

PORTABILITY (HARD RULE): the CLI and the ratatui TUI must compile and run natively on Termux/Android like every other non-GUI crate - a terminal app is IN scope, not exempt. Only the egui/eframe interface is a genuine GUI exemption and must be target-gated so the library still builds headless for aarch64-linux-android. Image decoding must be pure Rust with no C toolchain.

DESIGN: enum dispatch over axis types and trace strategies, no trait objects, no Box, no lifetime parameters. Offline and deterministic, consistent with the rest of KOVAN - no cloud, no ML service.
title: kovan-literature: graph digitiser module (CLI + TUI + egui, graphreader-style)

description:
No V&V case exists for the turbine at all. This is the primary gate on adiabatic_efficiency.

Spencer, R. C., Cotton, K. C., Cannon, C. N., 'A Method for Predicting the Performance of Steam Turbine-Generators ... 16,500 kW and Larger', ASME Paper 62-WA-209; J. Eng. Power 85 (1963) 249-298; revised July 1974. Gives efficiency correlations for the governing stage and the HP, IP and LP sections as functions of volumetric flow, pressure ratio and wetness (the paper's Figures 2-18).

ACCESS CAVEAT: the primary document was NOT obtained during the 2026-08-04 literature search; its contents are described here from secondary sources (the published ASME Discussion, and EBSILON's 'Component 122: Steam Turbine (SCC)' documentation). Obtain the primary paper before implementing — do not reconstruct the correlation from secondary descriptions.

Scope context: crates/tampines-steam-tables/docs/validation-scope-turbine-and-pipe.md section 3.1.
title: V&V: turbine section efficiency vs Spencer-Cotton-Cannon correlations

description:
Per docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md section 5: target PBMR-400 BEFORE HTR-10. It is the most completely specified open pebble-bed benchmark and it exercises exactly the coupling that has to be built. Reaching HTR-10 measured transients with an unvalidated bed model would be guessing.

SEQUENCE:
1. PBMR-400 OECD/NEA coupled benchmark — steady state, then depressurised and pressurised loss of cooling, then rod withdrawal.
2. HTR-10 initial criticality (critical loading height) from the IAEA HTGR benchmark programme.
3. HTR-10 safety demonstration tests — loss of forced cooling without scram, and control-rod withdrawal without scram. Expect digitised plots rather than tabulated data, and record the digitisation procedure and its uncertainty as part of provenance.

Per the V&V rule, documentation must carry BOTH methodology and results: the reference, the inputs, the pass criterion, AND the measured numbers with uncertainty and the date taken. Depends on the bed closures and the graphite feedback channel.

Report disagreement honestly. A documented mismatch is a result; a quietly loosened tolerance is not.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
HTR-10 thermal-hydraulic V&V targets, extracted 2026-08-11 from Gao, Z. and Shi, L. (2002), Thermal hydraulic calculation of the HTR-10 for the initial and equilibrium core, Nucl. Eng. Des. 218, 51-64, doi 10.1016/S0029-5493(02)00198-X. PROPRIETARY (Elsevier, all rights reserved) - catalogued at crates/kovan-literature/proprietary/papers/gao2002htr10th.json, gitignored. Cite it and implement from it; do NOT re-host the PDF.

This paper closes the gap that the VTB cannot: docs/reactor-scoping/vtb-findings.md records that VTB has NO HTR-10 thermal hydraulics at all. Gao and Shi supply calculated power, temperature and flow distributions for BOTH the initial and the equilibrium core.

QUANTITATIVE TARGETS TO VALIDATE AGAINST:
- Maximum fuel temperature 1046 C at 120 percent overload. This is the headline number to reproduce.
- HTR-10 maximum fuel temperature LIMIT is 1230 C under normal and accident conditions, per the experiment specification. NOTE this is NOT the 1600 C figure that appears throughout the modular-HTR literature (including the JRC book kugeler2017vhtr) - 1600 C is the generic coated-particle retention limit, 1230 C is HTR-10 own specified limit. Do not conflate them.
- Bypass flow through the gaps between graphite components is under 10 percent of rated flow. Any bed model that ignores bypass is therefore making a 10 percent error in core flow.
- Uncertainties the paper explicitly carries into the peak fuel temperature: non-uniform burnup, power distribution deviation, manufacturing deviation of fuel elements, graphite balls mixed with fuel balls in the initial core, and heat-transfer calculation deviation. A V&V comparison that ignores these is comparing a best-estimate to a conservative number.
- Initial core contains graphite balls mixed uniformly with fuel balls to suppress excess reactivity; the equilibrium core has none. These are two DIFFERENT validation cases, not one.

Confirms the operating point already taken from the IAEA benchmark: 10 MW, 3.0 MPa, 4.3 kg/s, 700 C outlet, 250 C inlet, feedwater 104 C, steam 440 C at 4.0 MPa.

title: HTR-10 V&V: PBMR-400 coupled benchmark first, then HTR-10 criticality and safety demonstration tests

description:
Maintainer chose to regenerate missing mirrors (2026-08-14). Shells out to 'python3 scripts/gen_api_docs.py <crate-dir-name>' per crate.

OFF BY DEFAULT, behind an explicit flag. It is not offline and not deterministic: needs a nightly toolchain (rustdoc JSON is nightly-only), the rustdoc-md binary, and a python3 interpreter, and it compiles the crate. Follow the precedent already set by 'kovan setup' in this same CLI, whose doc comment reads 'Explicit, online, desktop-scope convenience -- never run automatically, and has no bearing on the rest of kovan's offline/Android-clean operation'. Mirror that wording.

FAIL LOUDLY, NOT SILENTLY. If nightly or rustdoc-md or python3 is missing, say which one and what to run -- do not fall back to emitting a bundle that quietly lacks those crates.

BUDGET WARNING. Regenerating all 24 would add roughly 2.4 MB (~600k estimated tokens) to a corpus already 6.5x over budget. Only worth running for crates actually being selected. Consider restricting it to the crates named in --crates rather than every missing one.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
IMPLEMENTED but NOT EXERCISED. --regenerate-missing is wired and shells out to scripts/gen_api_docs.py with loud, named errors for a missing python3 / nightly / rustdoc-md. It has NOT been run: this host has no nightly toolchain or rustdoc-md installed, so the happy path is unverified. Do not describe it as working until someone runs it. Kept open for that reason.

Scope narrowed on build: it regenerates only crates named in --crates that lack a mirror, not all 24. Regenerating all of them would add ~2.4 MB to a corpus already 6.5x over budget for no benefit.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
CORRECTION 2026-08-14 -- the previous note on this bead was WRONG, and so were the hand-off and the commit message for b0fafebefc.

It claimed --regenerate-missing was untestable because 'this host has no nightly toolchain or rustdoc-md installed'. That was never checked. Both were installed all along: rustdoc-md v0.2.0 and nightly-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, plus python3.

Running it revealed the feature HAD NEVER WORKED. validate_selection() ran BEFORE regenerate(), so it rejected the selected crate for having no docs/api.md -- exactly the file the flag exists to create -- and returned before regeneration was reached. The flag was dead on arrival.

FIXED: the check is split around regeneration. validate_exists() (crate directory is real) runs first so a typo is caught before anything expensive; regenerate() runs; validate_documented() (mirror now present) runs after.

VERIFIED END TO END: 'kovan agent-docs-gen --crates kovan-common --regenerate-missing' generated crates/kovan-common/docs/api.md (47,279 bytes) via nightly rustdoc + rustdoc-md and bundled it -- core set AGENTS.md + _INDEX.md + kovan-common.api.md = 60,164 bytes, ~15,041 estimated tokens. Exit 0.

A CLAUDE.md hard rule now covers this: install rustdoc-md and nightly rather than routing around them, and check with 'which rustdoc-md' / 'rustup toolchain list' before claiming a tool is absent.

title: agent-docs: opt-in --regenerate-missing for the 24 crates with no api.md
